subject: Discovery recap: API decoupling & open-model shortlist for HelixMed
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Kapoor <sanjay.kapoor@helixmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: API decoupling & open-model shortlist for HelixMed

Thanks for taking the time today, Sanjay — appreciated the candid conversation. Below is a short recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

TL;DR
- Pain: Heavy dependence on OpenAI + Anthropic endpoints for core patient-facing summarization and coding assistance; rising per-token cost and brittle latency for peak hours.
- Goal: Decouple from proprietary APIs to an open-model stack (hosted/dedicated/private options) with equivalent output quality, lower unit cost, and enterprise-grade controls (PII handling + audit logs).

What we heard (pain points)
- Token spend: ~1.2B tokens/month across inference and embeddings, big spikes during daily morning windows.
- Latency/SLA: 95th percentile end-to-end latency currently ~1.2s on average for short responses, spikes to 4–6s during peak.
- Compliance: Must retain full audit trails and be able to limit model access to PHI-stripped contexts; SOC 2 + HIPAA posture is required.
- Vendor risk: Concerned about pricing and terms with upstream proprietary providers; want ability to run locally/on VPC for controlled workloads.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Frontend collects patient interactions, backend calls a middleware service that fans out to OpenAI (gpt-4o) for generation and Anthropic for safety/reranking.
- A light caching layer for embeddings; no KV cache for decoding; single-region (us-west) setup.

Success criteria (what 'good' looks like)
- Out-of-the-box parity with current quality on the 12 representative prompts we shared (precision and style).
- 30–50% reduction in per-token inference cost at target QPS, or predictable cost with reserved capacity.
- Ability to run sensitive workloads inside HelixMed VPC or our private deployment (data never leaves tenant-controlled infra).
- Auditability: per-request trace id, model versioning, and retention controls.

Initial compatibility notes / model shortlist (high-level)
- Candidate families to evaluate: Llama-derivative quantized variants (for cost), open high-capacity decoder models for parity. Need to test quality + hallucination profile against your prompt set.
- We will propose 3 model variants: a low-latency smaller quantized model, a mid-size balanced model, and a high-quality candidate for critical flows.

Immediate asks from your side
1) Share the SOC2 answers + any existing data classification documents (you mentioned you would attach SOC2 QAs).
2) Export of the top 12 prompt+response examples (anonymized) for our eval run.
3) Peak QPS and 95th latency targets for the migration cutover (helps sizing).

Proposed next steps
- I will circulate a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones: pilot scope, model evaluation, security review, and cutover runway. (see attachment: mutual-action-plan-v1.xlsx)
- Schedule 60-min technical deep-dive next week to walk infra/stack and run through evaluation requirements — suggest Tue 3/16 or Wed 3/17.
- We’ll run a quality sweep on the 12 prompts and share a short report + recommended model shortlist within 7 business days after we receive the prompts.

If this reads accurately, can you: (a) confirm 3/16 or 3/17 for the tech call, (b) send the SOC2 QAs and the anonymized prompt bundle, and (c) confirm any internal stakeholders we should include on the tech call?

Thanks again — excited to help HelixMed reduce risk while keeping the clinical QA high.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments referenced: mutual-action-plan-v1.xlsx

From: Sanjay Kapoor <sanjay.kapoor@helixmed.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: API decoupling & open-model shortlist for HelixMed

Vivek — thanks for the clear summary. This is exactly aligned with what we discussed. A few clarifications and attachments below.

Responses / clarifications
- Confirm token numbers: ~1.2B tokens/month average (we saw a 40% spike in Jan-Feb due to a product campaign). Embeddings are ~30% of the spend.
- Models in use today: OpenAI (gpt-4o for generation), Anthropic claude-2 for safety/re-rank. We rely on Anthropic for a final rerank/safety pass on clinical copy.
- PII/PHI handling: Anything flagged as PHI is stripped before sending to public endpoints today by our middleware — we would prefer to move that filtering upstream or to a private deployment if feasible.
- On-prem vs VPC: Priority is VPC-hosted for production critical flows; we may try a dedicated-hosted pilot for non-PHI traffic first.

Attachments included
- helixmed-soc2-answers.pdf (SOC2 questionnaire worksheet)
- helixmed-current-stack-diagram.png (simple infra diagram)

Questions for Redwood
- Can you share a rough sizing and cost band for the 3 model tiers you mentioned (pilot, mid, high-quality) — even a bucketed estimate is fine so we can budget?
- For Anthropic replacement: we rely on a re-ranker that is tuned to our moderation thresholds. Can your approach accommodate a reranking/safety pass in the pipeline?

Tech call windows
- 3/16 (Tue) 10–11am PT works for the infra team; 3/17 is slightly worse. Can you hold 3/16 10am PT?

Thanks — looping in our platform lead (platform@helixmed.com) for scheduling.

— Sanjay Kapoor
Head of Platform, HelixMed
Sanjay.Kapoor@helixmed.com

Ben / Monica — quick internal note and action items after Sanjay’s reply.

Key asks from HelixMed:
- Send MAP + model cost bands before the tech call on 3/16 (they need budget flags).
- We need to run an eval on their 12 prompts as soon as we receive them; coordinate with Applied ML for the scoring.
- Confirm support for a reranking safety pass that can be included post-generation (they use Anthropic today).

Action items
- Ben: please draft 3 cost bands (pilot | mid | high-quality) with rough monthly run-rate estimates for 1.2B tokens/month and peak QPS scenarios. Include hosted vs dedicated vs private price differentials. Target: EOD Fri 3/12.
- Monica: prep the eval pipeline checklist and confirm QA metrics (BLEU/ROUGE not sufficient — we’ll include clinical safety and hallucination checks). Also prepare a short runbook for the tech call. Target: Mon 3/15.
- Vivek: share MAP + tech call invite for 3/16 10am PT; include platform@helixmed.com and Sanjay.

I’ll follow up with a calendar invite in the next 20 minutes and attach the MAP + a short model comparison note.

Vivek
